proofs.proof_tex:
Under \(\texttt{ass:one-unsupported-row}\) and \(\texttt{ass:binary-free-row}\), the generalized unsupported-row objects specialize to
\[
 \mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}=\{rstar\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}
 =\{(1-q,q):0\leq q\leq1\}.
\]
After the structural Markovian conditions are separated, \(\texttt{def:model-class}\) and \(\texttt{def:finite-unsupported-model-class}\) still impose identical membership requirements in this specialization: the same finite schema and graph, the same source and target groundings, mutually independent exogenous noises, no exogenous relational parent, no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables, type-shared mechanisms, reproduction of \(Psrc\), and use of \(K\) at every positive-source-support key.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}=Mone,
 \qquad Q_{\mathrm{fin}}=Q.
\]
Replaying \(\texttt{def:multivariate-target-polynomial}\) at the unique free row \(p_{rstar}=(1-q,q)\) is exactly the replay defining \(F\).  This is also the equality supplied by \(\texttt{lem:polynomial-reduction}\), so
\[
 \Phi\bigl((1-q,q)\bigr)=F(q),
 \qquad 0\leq q\leq1.
\]
The specialization of \(\texttt{thm:sharp-finite-unsupported-rows}\) therefore gives
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])
 =\left[\min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q),\max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)\right],
\]
and its reverse inclusion is witnessed by compatible finite-noise, type-shared RSCMs.

It remains to identify these extrema with \(L\) and \(U\).  If \(F\) is nonconstant and \(c\in(0,1)\) is an optimizer, then for sufficiently small \(h>0\) the two one-sided difference quotients have opposite weak signs.  Since a polynomial is differentiable,
\[
 F'(c)
 =\lim_{h\downarrow0}\frac{F(c+h)-F(c)}{h}
 =\lim_{h\downarrow0}\frac{F(c)-F(c-h)}{h}
 =0.
\]
Thus every optimizer is either \(0\), \(1\), or a feasible distinct real root of \(F'\), and hence lies in \(Ccrit\) by \(\texttt{def:critical-candidates}\).  Conversely \(Ccrit\subseteq[0,1]\) and \(0,1\in Ccrit\).  Therefore
\[
 \min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\min_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=L,
 \qquad
 \max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\max_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=U.
\]
If \(F\) is constant, every value in \(F(Ccrit)\) is the same, and the same equalities follow from \(0,1\in Ccrit\).  This proves \(\Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U]\) without any comparator-domain assumption.

We now prove only the conditional comparator conclusions stated in the theorem.  Let \(\mathcal E_{\rho}\) denote the Ejaz--Bareinboim Definition~3.2 anchor class for the fixed causal problem, and let \(\mathcal E_5\) be its intersection with the domain satisfying the separately stated Section~5 assumptions~(I)--(III).  By the corrected \(\texttt{lem:ejaz-bareinboim-rho-markovian-scope}\), Definition~3.2 forbids exogenous relational parents but permits a non-relational exogenous parent to be shared only among attributes of the same instance.  The two structural restrictions recorded in \(\texttt{ass:no-exogenous-relational-parents}\) and \(\texttt{ass:no-shared-nonrelational-exogenous-parent}\) put every \(Mone\) model inside the Definition~3.2 anchor whenever the remaining anchor requirements are matched.  Section~5 has additional domain conditions.  In particular, its global relational-parent multiset bound is not implied by the fact that the finitely many listed source and target groundings have finite maximum degree.  Thus no inclusion \(Mone\subseteq\mathcal E_5\) is used unless it is supplied explicitly for the admissible skeleton family.

Assume now the inclusion required by the theorem's comparator clause, namely \(Mone\subseteq\mathcal E_5\), and suppose that \(F\) is nonconstant.  Then there exist \(q_1,q_2\in[0,1]\) such that \(F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)\).  Structural sharpness supplies \(M_1,M_2\in Mone\) with
\[
 Q(M_1)=F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)=Q(M_2).
\]
The inclusion gives \(M_1,M_2\in\mathcal E_5\), and the same two witnesses lie in every comparator class containing \(\mathcal E_5\).  Hence the query is not point identified in each such class.  This proves upward transfer only under the stated inclusion/intersection hypothesis.  Corollary~D.7 may be invoked to interpret the neural procedure's result only on \(\mathcal E_5\).  Whether that procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) or not, the structural argument already proved that \([L,U]\) is sharp for \(Mone\).  If a comparator class strictly contains \(Mone\), the inclusion supplies no upper or lower restriction on the additional models, so it cannot prove that \([L,U]\) is sharp there.

If \(F\) is constant, the structural part gives \(L=U\) on \(Mone\).  Equality of the comparator-compatible class with \(Mone\) transfers this singleton immediately.  Mere strict containment does not: constancy of a function on a subset says nothing about its values on new elements.  This proves the constant-case qualification.

Finally, unsupportedness alone does not force \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).  Consider an acyclic two-node target with a supported fair binary node \(A\), an unsupported binary node \(X\) with success probability \(q\), independent noises, no exogenous relational parents, no shared non-relational exogenous parent, and event \(B=\{A=X\}\).  Direct factorization gives
\[
 P(B\mid\operatorname{do}(a))
 =(1-q)\frac12+q\frac12=\frac12.
\]
The unsupported row is target relevant but cancels, so the causal query is point identified in this instance.  Type sharing is load bearing for the asserted one-parameter image: with two independent target nodes using the same unsupported binary key and the event of exactly one success, the shared-row map is
\[
 2q(1-q)\leq\frac12.
\]
If type sharing is removed while the other conditions are retained, occurrence-specific rows \(q_1=1\) and \(q_2=0\) make that event have probability one.  These finite examples verify both the cancellation claim and the necessity of the common coordinate \(q\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Within the fully Markovian class \(Mone\), the compatible causal set is exactly
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U].
\]
Every comparison with the Ejaz--Bareinboim procedure is restricted to the intersection of its Definition~3.2 \(\rho\)-Markovian anchor class with the domain satisfying the separately stated Section~5 assumptions~(I)--(III).  Finiteness of the listed source and target groundings does not by itself establish the required global bound on relational-parent multiset size.  If \(F\) is nonconstant and \(Mone\) is included in that intersection, nonidentification transfers to every comparator class containing this intersection.  A return value \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) from the complete procedure on that domain does not alter the equality \(\Theta=[L,U]\) for \(Mone\), but \([L,U]\) is not asserted to be sharp for a strict comparator superclass.  If \(F\) is constant, then \(L=U\) identifies the query over \(Mone\); this singleton conclusion transfers only when the comparator-compatible class equals \(Mone\), not merely when it contains \(Mone\).  The unsupported status of \(rstar\) alone does not imply \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The structural sharp-set equality is unchanged. The comparator clauses are narrowed to the published anchor/Section 5 intersection and now require explicit class inclusion before upward transfer; finite listed groundings no longer masquerade as a global bounded-parent condition.

proposed_assumptions.condition: No exogenous variable in any admissible source or target grounding has a relational parent.
proposed_assumptions.reason: This is one of the published Markovian anchor restrictions and was not implied by independent sampled noises.

proposed_assumptions.condition: No non-relational exogenous variable is a parent of two distinct ground endogenous variables.
proposed_assumptions.reason: The structural class used by the sharpness proofs excludes all shared non-relational exogenous parents; this cannot be inferred from mutual independence of distinct noise variables.
proposed_assumptions.standard_or_novel: standard: Fully Markovian absence of shared non-relational exogenous parents (EjazBareinboim2026RSCM)

proposed_assumptions.condition: There exists one finite integer bound such that, for every admissible skeleton over \(S\) and \(G\) and every ground endogenous variable in that skeleton, the cardinality of its instantiated relational-parent multiset is at most that bound.
proposed_assumptions.reason: This is a comparator-only Section 5 domain condition. It is global over admissible skeletons and is not a premise of the structural image or certificate results.

proposed.condition: All exogenous noise variables appearing in every source and target grounding are mutually independent.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Noise independence is one condition and does not by itself exclude a shared exogenous parent, so the parent restrictions are recorded separately.

proposed.name: Finite-unsupported-row compatible RSCM class
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\) is the class of finite RSCMs over \(S\) and \(G\) that induce the source groundings \(Rsrc\) and target grounding \(\rho\) encoded by \(Ictx\), have mutually independent exogenous noises, have no exogenous relational parent and no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables, have type-shared finite mechanisms, reproduce \(Psrc\), use the recovered rows \(K\) at every target-relevant positive-source-support key, and leave precisely the target-relevant keys in \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}\) unrestricted over their native finite outcome alphabets.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The generalized structural class receives the same explicit fully Markovian decomposition as the one-row class and remains independent of the comparator-only global bound.

Polynomial programming yields numerical sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds and confidence-region relaxations for discrete causal queries.
Untrusted algebraic root certificates can be checked skeptically by verified univariate CAD and Sturm--Tarski computations.
Root counting and interval subdivision decide univariate polynomial relation systems soundly and completely in PVS.

prose_updates.tldr: For any finite family of target-relevant unsupported finite-categorical shared rows, the fully Markovian relational causal set is exactly the compact interval obtained as the image of an explicit rational polynomial over the product of row simplices, with finite-noise endpoint witnesses. The one unsupported binary row remains the tractable specialization with exact algebraic certificates. Here fully Markovian means mutually independent exogenous noises, no exogenous relational parents, and no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground variables. Comparison with Ejaz--Bareinboim is only on the intersection of their Definition~3.2 \(\rho\)-Markovian anchor and their Section~5 assumptions~(I)--(III); the global parent-multiset bound is not inferred from the finitely listed groundings. Nonconstant \(F\) transfers nonidentification only when inclusion in that intersection is explicit, and neither the sharp interval nor a singleton transfers to a strict superclass. Supported-row boxes use \(\delta_{\times}=1-\prod_r(1-\epsilon_r)^{m_r}\), while the frozen exhaustive-assignment grammar, rather than relational treewidth itself, accounts for the \(2^k\) incidence witness.

project_justification.gap: Complete relational identification on the published anchor/Section 5 intersection does not return the exact compatible causal range after nonidentification. Generic polynomial bounds also do not realize every product-simplex point by a type-shared fully Markovian RSCM or certify the relational derivation and endpoint models.
project_justification.niche: Finitely many unsupported finite-categorical rows admit an exact structural reduction on a fully Markovian no-shared-parent class; the one-binary-row specialization additionally admits efficient exact univariate algebraic certification.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the multivariate structural sharp image and finite-noise endpoint witnesses without a global skeleton-degree assumption, supplies a skeptical univariate certificate, and states published-comparator consequences only on the explicit Definition~3.2/Section~5 intersection.

prose_updates.related_work: Ejaz and Bareinboim's Definition~3.2 gives the \(\rho\)-Markovian anchor: it excludes exogenous relational parents and allows a shared non-relational exogenous parent only for attributes of the same instance. Their Section~5 completeness and neural results apply separately under assumptions~(I)--(III), including finite observed domains and one uniform relational-parent-multiset bound over every admissible skeleton; Corollary~D.7 is the version-two neural correctness result. The present exact image is proved for a fully Markovian subclass with mutually independent exogenous noises and no shared non-relational exogenous parent, without assuming that global bound. Consequently, comparison is restricted to the intersection with the published Section~5 domain. A nonconstant image proves nonidentification upward only when the fully Markovian compatible class is explicitly included in that intersection; neither its sharp interval nor a constant-polynomial singleton transfers to a strict superclass. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim provide canonical finite-SCM polynomial programs, and Duarte et al. provide general numerical polynomial bounds and confidence-constraint relaxations; neither supplies this relational product-simplex realization theorem, exact univariate relational certificate, or multiplicative labeled-occurrence enclosure. Li, Passmore, and Paulson, Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle, and Tsigaridas and Emiris supply the skeptical algebraic and root-isolation substrate. Hutschenreiter, Baier, and Klein identify a polynomial explicit-univariate model-checking core. Rossetto and Antonucci construct attaining models for order-based nonrelational bounds, but their witnesses do not impose the present type-shared fully Markovian semantics.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Structural soundness, compact interval form, endpoint attainment, and the finite breakpoint atom-count bound are proved for any finite family of unsupported finite-categorical rows in fully observed, acyclic, type-shared RSCMs with mutually independent exogenous noises, no exogenous relational parents, and no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables. These structural results do not assume a global bound on relational-parent multiset size. That bound is a comparator-only condition in the Ejaz--Bareinboim Section~5 domain and cannot be inferred from the finite source and target groundings. All comparator claims are restricted to the intersection of that domain with the Definition~3.2 anchor; nonidentification transfers only under explicit class inclusion, and sharp ranges or singleton identification transfer only under class equality. Exact derivative-root optimization, algebraic endpoint comparison, polynomial-size certificates, the sharp optimizer-degree guarantee, and the at-most-two algebraic-noise-mass guarantee remain specific to one unsupported binary row. Efficient exact multivariate optimization, compact circuit-level incidence, conditional postintervention queries, exact nuisance-box projection, and empirical usefulness beyond the documented N3 example remain open. The sampling enclosure is conservative and uses \(\delta_{\times}\leq\min\{1,\sum_rm_r\epsilon_r\}\).
